blogTitle: Solving Moisture Problems with Safe Bathtub Decor Ideas
videoTitle: Solving Moisture Problems with Safe Bathtub Decor Ideas
script:
Solving Moisture Problems with Safe Bathtub Decor Ideas

[warmly] Okay — if you've ever dealt with damp, musty smells, or mould creeping in around your bathtub… this one's for YOU.

Moisture problems in the bathroom can lead to mould growth, bad odours, and actual DAMAGE to your walls — so it's worth taking seriously.

First step — actually know how HUMID your bathroom is… a simple hygrometer tells you straight away.

Anything consistently above 60% humidity… that's when mould and mildew really start to take hold, you know?

Poor ventilation, leaks around the tub, absorbent materials… honestly, it's usually a COMBINATION of things causing the problem.

Hidden leaks behind the tub or under tiles are sneaky — they can let mould get a real FOOTHOLD before you even notice.

Now — the fun part… let's talk SAFE bathtub decor ideas that actually look incredible AND resist moisture.

Choose non-porous, quick-drying materials — think ceramic, teak, bamboo… things that REPEL moisture rather than soak it up.

[excited] And plants! Moisture-loving plants like ferns or peace lilies actually HELP balance humidity — and they look gorgeous.

A little tip I love: place plants on a ceramic or bamboo saucer — never directly on a wooden surface… it'll warp over time.

Here's the thing about maintaining a moisture-FREE bathroom — regular cleaning is honestly non-negotiable.

Wiping down tiles and surfaces after every shower… sounds simple, but it makes a HUGE difference to stopping mould before it starts.

Inspect your decorative accessories regularly too — even the prettiest items can harbour moisture if you're not checking them.

Ventilation is EVERYTHING — your exhaust fan or a cracked window after a shower does more than any product ever could.

[gently] Run your extractor fan during AND for at least 20 minutes after a shower… that's when most of the humidity actually escapes.

Now for the COSY bit — creating a really inviting atmosphere around your bathtub without making moisture worse.

For lighting… waterproof LED options or a lamp placed OUTSIDE the splash zone give you that warm glow without the risk.

Trust me — accessories like over-bath caddies and wall hooks keep your lovely things OFF wet surfaces… so they actually LAST.

[warmly] Okay this is one of my FAVOURITES — adding wall art to your bathroom is honestly the easiest way to pull the whole look together.

Non-slip mats are a MUST in wet areas — they're a safety essential, and honestly they can look really chic too.

For safe décor accessories — look for quick-drying, non-porous finishes… and always check that framed art has a SEALED backing.

[sighs] Honestly… a few small, smart choices and your bathroom can feel like a proper SANCTUARY — dry, safe, and beautiful.

These three prints are a gorgeous finishing touch — soft florals that bring warmth to a bathroom without ever feeling heavy.

And if you want something a little bolder — this framed set of three gives your bathroom wall a really POLISHED, curated feel.

This smaller set of two is PERFECT if you've got a tighter wall space — it still makes a real impact without overwhelming the room.

And this single statement print… sometimes ONE really considered piece is all a bathroom NEEDS to feel complete.

Did you know styling your home doesn't have to be guesswork?

We've built a free set of Home Decor tools and styling guides…

From colour theory and design principles to gallery wall layouts and art sizing. Download them all from our site!

Find all you need to transform your home into a calming oasis!

Happy Decorating!

Muted sage-green towels hang neatly from a matte-black rail. A framed set of three black-and-white botanical prints hangs above a low wooden stool holding a ceramic soap dish and a single dried stem in a small vase.
